claim: Microtubules segregate chromosomes by attaching to macromolecular kinetochores.
source: Microtubules segregate chromosomes by attaching to macromolecular kinetochores.
evidence: This is a foundational statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific consensus about chromosome segregation.

claim: Only microtubule-end attached kinetochores can be pulled apart.
source: Only microtubule-end attached kinetochores can be pulled apart
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge in the field and is presented as a known fact in the abstract.

claim: End-on attachments are rapidly stabilised by spatially-restricted delivery of PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80.
source: end-on attachments are rapidly stabilised by spatially-restricted delivery of PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80, a core kinetochore-microtubule linker
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study presented in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: PP1 is delivered by the evolutionarily conserved tail of Astrin.
source: PP1 is delivered by the evolutionarily conserved tail of Astrin
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the role of Astrin's C-terminal tail and bioinformatic analysis showing evolutionary conservation.

claim: Astrin-mediated PP1 delivery promotes Astrin's own enrichment creating a highly-responsive positive feedback.
source: this promotes Astrin's own enrichment creating a highly-responsive positive feedback, independent of biorientation
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that PP1 delivery enhances Astrin enrichment at kinetochores.

claim: The positive feedback mechanism for Astrin enrichment is independent of biorientation.
source: this promotes Astrin's own enrichment creating a highly-responsive positive feedback, independent of biorientation
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments using monopolar spindles that cannot biorient kinetochores.

claim: Abrogating Astrin:PP1-delivery disrupts attachment stability.
source: Abrogating Astrin:PP1-delivery disrupts attachment stability
evidence: This is supported by experimental data using Astrin mutants that cannot bind PP1.

claim: Inhibiting Aurora-B does not rescue attachment defects caused by disrupting Astrin:PP1-delivery.
source: which is not rescued by inhibiting Aurora-B, an attachment destabiliser
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments combining Aurora-B inhibition with Astrin mutant expression.

claim: Artificially tethering PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80 reverses attachment defects caused by Astrin:PP1-docking mutants.
source: but is reversed by artificially tethering PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments using GBP-PP1 fusion proteins to deliver PP1 to specific locations.

claim: Constitutive Astrin:PP1-delivery disrupts chromosome congression and segregation.
source: Constitutive Astrin:PP1-delivery disrupts chromosome congression and segregation
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments with premature and constitutive PP1 delivery.

claim: Astrin-PP1 mediates a dynamic 'lock' that selectively and rapidly stabilises end-on attachments.
source: Thus, Astrin-PP1 mediates a dynamic 'lock' that selectively and rapidly stabilises end-on attachments, independent of biorientation, and ensures proper chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations throughout the study.

claim: Chromosome segregation cannot be initiated until all chromosomes are properly attached to microtubules from opposing spindle poles.
source: Chromosome segregation can not be initiated until all chromosomes are properly attached to microtubules from opposing spindle poles - a state called biorientation.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of cell division.

claim: A macromolecular structure called the kinetochore assembles on centromeric DNA to mediate and monitor chromosome-microtubule attachments.
source: To mediate and monitor chromosome-microtubule attachments, a macromolecular structure, the kinetochore (KT) assembles on centromeric DNA (reviewed in Conti et al., 2017; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Kinetochores are first captured along microtubule-walls (immature lateral attachment) and then brought to microtubule-ends (mature end-on attachment).
source: Kinetochores are first captured along microtubule-walls (immature lateral attachment) and then brought to microtubule-ends (mature end-on attachment), by a multi-step end-on conversion process (Tanaka et al., 2005; Shrestha and Draviam, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Only end-on attachments can impart pulling forces to segregate chromosomes apart.
source: Only end-on attachments can impart pulling forces to segregate chromosomes apart
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by the cited literature.

claim: In the absence of end-on attachments, checkpoint proteins are retained at the kinetochore which prevents premature chromosome segregation.
source: in the absence of end-on attachments, checkpoint proteins are retained at the kinetochore which prevents premature chromosome segregation (reviewed in Musacchio and Desai, 2017; Cheeseman, 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Aurora-B-mediated phosphorylation of Ndc80 destabilises microtubule binding.
source: Aurora-B-mediated phosphorylation of Ndc80 (a core KT-MT linker) destabilises microtubule binding (Miller et al., 2008; Guimaraes et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PP1 recruited by KNL1/hSPC105 is not essential for stabilising attachments.
source: but the phosphatase PP1 recruited by KNL1/hSPC105 to counteract Aurora-B for checkpoint silencing (Nijenhuis et al., 2014; Meadows et al., 2011; Rosenberg et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2010) is not essential for stabilising attachments (Shrestha et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KNL1-recruited PP1 is not essential for segregation accuracy.
source: or segregation accuracy (Zhang et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: When end-on attachments form, checkpoint proteins BubR1, Bub1 and MPS1 are either removed from or reduced at kinetochores.
source: When end-on attachments form, the checkpoint proteins BubR1, Bub1 and MPS1 that influence attachments are all either removed from or reduced at kinetochores (Shrestha and Draviam, 2013; Kuhn and Dumont, 2017; O'Connell et al., 2008; Hiruma et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Astrin-SKAP complex is recruited to kinetochores when end-on attachments form.
source: Simultaneously, the Astrin-SKAP complex is recruited to kinetochores (Shrestha and Draviam, 2013; Kuhn and Dumont, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Astrin-SKAP binds to microtubules through multiple contact points.
source: Astrin-SKAP binds to microtubules through multiple contact points (Friese et al., 2016; Kern et al., 2017; Dunsch et al., 2011; Tamura et al., 2015; Huang et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2012; Maffini et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the absence of Astrin-SKAP, end-on attachments form but are not stably maintained.
source: In the absence of Astrin-SKAP, the end-on conversion process is disrupted; end-on attachments form but are not stably maintained (Shrestha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: YFP-Astrin forms either a low-intensity 'sleeve' decorating the outer-kinetochore and associated microtubule-end or a high-intensity 'crescent' decorating the outer-kinetochore alone.
source: YFP-Astrin forms either a low-intensity 'sleeve' decorating the outer-kinetochore and associated microtubule-end or a high-intensity 'crescent' decorating the outer-kinetochore alone (Figure 1A)
evidence: This is directly observed in live-cell imaging experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: YFP-Astrin sleeve gradually converts into brighter YFP-Astrin crescent.
source: Tracking the fate of Astrin -sleeves and -crescents in cells co-expressing YFP-Astrin and CENP-B-DsRed, showed a gradual conversion of YFP-Astrin sleeve into brighter YFP-Astrin crescent (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both Astrin-crescents and sleeves are found at the outer-kinetochore.
source: To confirm that both Astrin-crescents and sleeves are found at the outer-kinetochore, we analysed YFP-Astrin localisation in cells co-expressing Nuf2-CFP, a bonafide outer-kinetochore marker. Overlap with Nuf2-CFP signal was partial in Astrin-sleeves and complete in Astrin-crescents, confirming the outer-kinetochore localisation of Astrin prior to biorientation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is confirmed through colocalization experiments with Nuf2-CFP shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The C-termini of both Ndc80 and Astrin are within a 5 nm distance.
source: FRET signals were prominent only in cells co-expressing C-terminal fluorescent protein tags for both Ndc80 and Astrin (Figure 1C,D), indicating that the C-termini of both proteins are within a 5 nm distance, expected for FRET (Müller et al., 2013).
evidence: This is demonstrated through FRET microscopy experiments shown in Figure 1C,D and supported by citation to FRET methodology.

claim: Cells co-expressing YFP-Astrin and Nuf2-CFP did not show prominent FRET signals.
source: In contrast, cells co-expressing YFP-Astrin and Nuf2-CFP did not show prominent FRET signals (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B), confirming that Astrin is recruited near Ndc80 in a specific orientation at the kinetochore.
evidence: This is demonstrated through FRET microscopy experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: The C-terminus of Astrin resides proximal to the C-terminus of Ndc80.
source: Second, the C-terminus of Astrin resides proximal to the C-terminus of Ndc80 ideally positioned to strengthen kinetochore-microtubule bridging after the formation of end-on attachments (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is inferred from FRET data and illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: For Astrin recruitment at kinetochores, its C-terminal 694–1193 a.a is sufficient.
source: For Astrin recruitment at kinetochores, its C-terminal 694–1193 a.a is sufficient (Kern et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: For Astrin recruitment at kinetochores, 851–1193 a.a is essential.
source: and 851–1193 a.a is essential (Dunsch et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Removing 70 amino acids (1123–1193 a.a) of the unstructured region abrogated Astrin's kinetochore enrichment as crescents.
source: Removing 70 amino acids (1123–1193 a.a) of the unstructured region (YFP-Astrin ∆70) abrogated Astrin's kinetochore enrichment as crescents; the deletion mutant was either present as sleeves or completely absent at the kinetochore, but was normally present on spindle microtubules and poles (Figure 2B,C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments with the Astrin ∆70 mutant shown in Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In cells expressing YFP-Astrin ∆70 mutant, SKAP failed to localise at the kinetochore but not spindle microtubules.
source: Moreover, in cells expressing YFP-Astrin ∆70 mutant (Figure 2B), SKAP failed to localise at the kinetochore but not spindle microtubules
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The 70 a.a long Astrin tail is important for targeting the entire Astrin-SKAP complex to the kinetochore-microtubule interface.
source: revealing an important role for the 70 a.a long Astrin tail in targeting the entire Astrin-SKAP complex to the kinetochore-microtubule interface
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that SKAP fails to localize to kinetochores in Astrin ∆70 expressing cells.

claim: Cells expressing either Astrin-WT or -∆70 displayed bipolar spindles.
source: While Astrin depleted cells displayed multipolar spindles as reported (Thein et al., 2007), cells expressing either Astrin-WT or -∆70 displayed bipolar spindles, indicating a successful rescue of the multipolar spindle phenotype seen in the absence of Astrin.
evidence: This is demonstrated through spindle morphology analysis in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The kinetochore pool of Astrin-SKAP is dispensable for bipolar spindle maintenance.
source: We conclude the kinetochore pool of Astrin-SKAP is dispensable for bipolar spindle maintenance.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that Astrin-∆70 mutant rescues bipolar spindle formation.

claim: Cells expressing Astrin-∆70 mutant showed a delayed anaphase onset compared to Astrin-WT.
source: Analysis of the time taken from Nuclear Envelope Break Down (NEBD) to anaphase onset, using YFP-Astrin signal on the spindle, showed a delayed anaphase onset in cells expressing Astrin-∆70 mutant compared to Astrin-WT
evidence: This is demonstrated through time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Spindle bipolarity and chromosome alignment or congression were unperturbed in Astrin-∆70 mutant expressing cells.
source: spindle bipolarity and chromosome alignment or congression were however unperturbed in mutant expressing cells (Figure 2F,G)
evidence: This is observed in time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Kinetochore-bound Astrin is required for timely anaphase, but not the congression of chromosomes or the maintenance of bipolar spindles.
source: In summary, kinetochore-bound Astrin is required for timely anaphase, but not the congression of chromosomes or the maintenance of bipolar spindles.
evidence: This is concluded from multiple experimental observations with Astrin mutants.

claim: The C-terminal tail of Astrin enables the selective recognition of end-on attached kinetochores and the timely onset of chromosome segregation.
source: The C-terminal tail of Astrin enables the selective recognition of end-on attached kinetochores and the timely onset of chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that the ∆70 mutant fails to enrich at kinetochores and delays anaphase.

claim: A bioinformatic search identified a putative PP1-docking motif RVxF in the unstructured C-terminal tail of Astrin.
source: This revealed a putative PP1-docking motif RVxF, previously reported in KNL1 (Bajaj et al., 2018).
evidence: This is identified through bioinformatic analysis and supported by citation to previous work on PP1-docking motifs.

claim: A bioinformatic search could identify Astrin elsewhere in Bilateria using the unstructured C-terminal tail.
source: Importantly, using the unstructured C-terminal tail, a bioinformatic search could identify Astrin elsewhere in Bilateria (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Source data 1)
evidence: This is demonstrated through bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The incidence of YFP-Astrin-4A crescents was significantly reduced compared to YFP-Astrin-WT crescents.
source: The incidence of YFP-Astrin-4A crescents was significantly reduced compared to YFP-Astrin-WT crescents (Figure 3A,B; Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) in congressed kinetochores of metaphase cells
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of kinetochore localization shown in Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The incidence of Astrin sleeves at congressed kinetochores was significantly increased in cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT.
source: However, the incidence of Astrin sleeves at congressed kinetochores was significantly increased in cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The RVxF motif is critical for enriching but not the initial recruitment of Astrin at the kinetochore.
source: These findings show that the RVxF motif is critical for enriching but not the initial recruitment of Astrin at the kinetochore.
evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin-4A can form sleeves but not crescents.

claim: Cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A showed a striking delay in anaphase onset compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT.
source: Tracking mitosis in YFP-Astrin-4A expressing cells treated with Astrin siRNA showed a striking delay in anaphase onset, compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: The delay in anaphase onset in Astrin-4A expressing cells occurred despite the normal completion of chromosome congression at the spindle equator.
source: This delay in anaphase onset was despite the normal completion of chromosome congression at the spindle equator (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is observed in time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MG132-treated metaphase cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing YFP-Astrin-4A maintained a bipolar spindle and aligned chromosomes similar to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT.
source: In agreement, MG132-treated metaphase cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing YFP-Astrin-4A maintained a bipolar spindle and aligned chromosomes similar to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through fixed-cell analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: The PP1 docking RVxF motif is dispensable for spindle bipolarity and chromosome congression but is crucial for the enrichment of Astrin-crescents and normal timing of anaphase.
source: In conclusion, the PP1 docking RVxF motif is dispensable for spindle bipolarity and chromosome congression but is crucial for the enrichment of Astrin-crescents and normal timing of anaphase.
evidence: This is concluded from multiple experimental observations with the Astrin-4A mutant.

claim: In Astrin-4A expressing cells, dim kinetochore-crescents gradually declined into Astrin-sleeves (referred as, blinking).
source: In Astrin-4A expressing cells, dim kinetochore-crescents gradually declined into Astrin-sleeves (referred as, blinking; Figure 3E)
evidence: This is observed in high-resolution time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Astrin-WT crescents were retained brightly at congressed kinetochores.
source: In contrast, Astrin-WT crescents were retained brightly at congressed kinetochores (Figure 3E)
evidence: This is observed in high-resolution time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Astrin-4A-expressing cells displayed multiple blinking events within a short 60 s window.
source: Unlike Astrin-WT-expressing cells, Astrin-4A-expressing cells displayed multiple blinking events within a short 60 s window, demonstrating compromised kinetochore life-time for YFP-Astrin-4A (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The putative PP1-docking motif is essential for the maintenance of Astrin-crescents.
source: We conclude that the putative PP1-docking motif is not essential for the initial arrival of Astrin sleeves at kinetochores; it is essential for the maintenance of Astrin-crescents
evidence: This is concluded from observations of Astrin-4A dynamics at kinetochores.

claim: Inter-kinetochore distances were significantly reduced in cells expressing Astrin-4A compared to Astrin-WT.
source: Despite normal kinetochore alignment at the spindle equator, inter-kinetochore distances between Astrin crescents were significantly reduced in cells expressing Astrin-4A compared to Astrin-WT (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is measured from live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Average inter-kinetochore distances were significantly reduced in cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT.
source: Measuring distances between CENP-B-DsRed pairs confirmed a significant reduction in average inter-kinetochore distances of cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A compared to YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B)
evidence: This is measured from time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Taxol treatment induced no changes in the levels of YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 at kinetochores.
source: Taxol treatment induced no changes in the levels of YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 at kinetochores (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through fixed-cell analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claim: Reduced microtubule-mediated pulling is a consequence, rather than the cause, of the reduced life-time of Astrin-4A at kinetochores.
source: We conclude that reduced microtubule-mediated pulling is a consequence, rather than the cause, of the reduced life-time of Astrin-4A at kinetochores.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that Taxol treatment does not rescue Astrin-4A localization.

claim: PP1γ enriches at the outer-kinetochore.
source: PP1γ enriches at the outer-kinetochore (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Cells co-expressing Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ displayed prominent FRET signals only on those kinetochores that retained both Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ.
source: Cells co-expressing Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ displayed prominent FRET signals only on those kinetochores that retained both Astrin-CFP and YFP-PP1γ (cyan arrow; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is observed in FRET microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The C-terminus of Astrin and PP1γ are recruited at the kinetochore within a FRET distance of 5 nm between the CFP and YFP probes.
source: These studies show that the C-terminus of Astrin and PP1γ are recruited at the kinetochore within a FRET distance of 5 nm between the CFP and YFP probes (Müller et al., 2013), suggesting a direct interaction between the tail of Astrin and PP1 at the outer kinetochore.
evidence: This is concluded from FRET measurements and supported by citation to FRET methodology.

claim: Astrin and PP1 interact at the outer-kinetochore, and this interaction is dynamic.
source: We conclude that Astrin and PP1 interact at the outer-kinetochore, and this interaction is dynamic.
evidence: This is concluded from FRET observations showing variable FRET signals at different kinetochores.

claim: Astrin isoforms can interact with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in Control siRNA treated mitotic cell lysates.
source: Immunoblotting using anti-Astrin antibodies showed that Astrin isoforms can interact with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in Control siRNA treated mitotic cell lysates, revealing a specific interaction between Astrin and PP1γ (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through pulldown assays shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Astrin interacts with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in two independent repeats of recombinant protein purification and pull down experiments.
source: Moreover, quantifying the ratio of Astrin band intensities in pull down lane relative to input lane of control siRNA treated cell lysates confirm that Astrin interacts with GST-PP1γ, but not GST, in two independent repeats of recombinant protein purification and pull down experiments (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is quantified from pulldown assay data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Astrin and PP1 interact with each other.
source: In summary, in vivo FRET studies reveal a dynamic and spatially restricted interaction between Astrin and PP1 at kinetochores. In vitro pull-down studies show a specific interaction between GST-PP1 but not GST. Based on these in vivo and in vitro studies we conclude that Astrin and PP1 interact with each other.
evidence: This is concluded from both FRET and pulldown experiments.

claim: The Astrin-CFP 4A mutant expressing cells present severely reduced FRET signals compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells.
source: However, using those timepoints when the Astrin-4A mutant was transiently enriched at the kinetochore, we could quantitatively establish that the Astrin-CFP 4A mutant expressing cells present severely reduced FRET signals compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through FRET measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The Astrin-CFP 4A mutant does not interact normally with YFP-PP1γ at kinetochores.
source: These live-cell studies show that the Astrin-CFP 4A mutant does not interact normally with YFP-PP1γ at kinetochores.
evidence: This is concluded from FRET measurements with the 4A mutant.

claim: Cells expressing Astrin mutant (4A or ∆70) displayed significantly fewer end-on attached kinetochores compared to cells expressing Astrin-WT.
source: Compared to cells expressing Astrin-WT, cells expressing Astrin mutant (4A or ∆70) displayed significantly fewer end-on attached kinetochores.
evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Laterally-attached kinetochores, and not detached kinetochores, were significantly increased in Astrin mutant-expressing cells.
source: Importantly, laterally-attached kinetochores, and not detached kinetochores, were significantly increased in Astrin mutant-expressing cells (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Astrin mutant-expressing cells are able to retain kinetochores along microtubule-walls but they cannot maintain kinetochores at microtubule-ends.
source: Thus, Astrin mutant-expressing cells are able to retain kinetochores along microtubule-walls but they cannot maintain kinetochores at microtubule-ends, similar to Astrin depleted cells (Shrestha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is concluded from attachment status analysis and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The kinetochore pool of Astrin is important for the selective stabilisation of end-on attachments.
source: This reveals that the kinetochore pool of Astrin is important for the selective stabilisation of end-on attachments.
evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin mutants fail to maintain end-on attachments.

claim: The incidence of Astrin-crescents was dramatically reduced in monopolar spindles of cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70, compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT.
source: In agreement, the incidence of Astrin-crescents was dramatically reduced in monopolar spindles of cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70, compared to cells expressing YFP-Astrin-WT (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is quantified from monopolar spindle analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Astrin:PP1 interaction is required specifically to maintain end-on, but not lateral, attachments independent of biorientation status.
source: These monopolar spindle studies together show that Astrin:PP1 interaction is required specifically to maintain end-on, but not lateral, attachments independent of biorientation status.
evidence: This is concluded from monopolar spindle experiments showing selective defects in end-on attachments.

claim: Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1 is not required for chromosome congression.
source: Thus, although Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1 is not required for chromosome congression (Figure 2D,E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D), it is crucial for the stable maintenance of end-on attachments (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin mutants can congress chromosomes but fail to maintain end-on attachments.

claim: Metaphase cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 mutant displayed prominent Mad2 or ZW10 signals in a subset of congressed kinetochores.
source: In contrast, metaphase cells expressing YFP-Astrin-4A or -∆70 mutant displayed prominent Mad2 or ZW10 signals in a subset of congressed kinetochores (Figure 5D,E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5D,E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There is an increased incidence of spindle checkpoint signalling in a small proportion of congressed kinetochores in cells expressing either of the two Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif.
source: These data indicate an increased incidence of spindle checkpoint signalling in a small proportion of congressed kinetochores in cells expressing either of the two Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif.
evidence: This is concluded from checkpoint protein localization analysis.

claim: Chromosome alignment at the spindle equator (i.e., congression efficiency) is not severely perturbed in Astrin mutant expressing cells.
source: As expected from low resolution time-lapse studies (Figures 2 and 3), chromosome alignment at the spindle equator (i.e., congression efficiency) is not severely perturbed in Astrin mutant expressing cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through congression efficiency analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The stable maintenance of end-on attachments, but not chromosome congression, requires the evolutionarily conserved PP1-docking motif in Astrin.
source: Thus, the stable maintenance of end-on attachments, but not chromosome congression, requires the evolutionarily conserved PP1-docking motif in Astrin.
evidence: This is concluded from multiple experimental observations with Astrin mutants.

claim: The levels of DSN1 pSer100 are reduced at kinetochores in cells expressing Astrin WT compared to Astrin 4A or -∆70 mutant.
source: Immunostaining of cells using phospho-specific antibodies against DSN1 pSer100 show that the levels of DSN1 pSer100 are reduced at kinetochores in cells expressing Astrin WT compared to Astrin 4A or -∆70 mutant (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: There is an increase in phosphorylated DSN1 signals in cells expressing Astrin 4A or -∆70 compared to Astrin WT.
source: Quantitative analysis of phospho-signal positive kinetochores and integrated kinetochore signal intensities confirm an increase in phosphorylated DSN1 signals in cells expressing Astrin 4A or -∆70 compared to Astrin WT (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: This is quantified from immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: Dsn1 phosphorylation status changes as a direct or indirect downstream target of Astrin-PP1 at kinetochores.
source: These findings show changes in Dsn1 phosphorylation status as a direct or indirect downstream target of Astrin-PP1 at kinetochores.
evidence: This is concluded from observations of DSN1 phosphorylation changes in Astrin mutant expressing cells.

claim: Co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ fully rescued the kinetochore enrichment defect in both Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif.
source: Nevertheless, co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ fully rescued the kinetochore enrichment defect in both Astrin mutants lacking the PP1-docking motif: both Astrin-∆70-GFP and Astrin-4A-GFP were enriched as bright crescents at the kinetochore when co-expressed with mCherry-GBP-PP1γ (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through rescue experiments shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: No rescue of the localisation defect was observed when Astrin-∆70 or −4A was fused to an N-terminal YFP tag in mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells.
source: Importantly, no rescue of the localisation defect was observed when Astrin-∆70 or −4A was fused to an N-terminal YFP tag in mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through rescue experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The kinetochore enrichment of Astrin is dependent on spatially-defined delivery of PP1 phosphatase at Astrin's C-terminus.
source: These studies show that the kinetochore enrichment of Astrin is dependent on spatially-defined delivery of PP1 phosphatase at Astrin's C-terminus (Figure 6C), which we show is proximal to the C-terminus of Ndc80 (Figure 1).
evidence: This is concluded from rescue experiments showing position-dependent effects of PP1 delivery.

claim: Cells co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ and Astrin-∆70-GFP or −4A-GFP display cold stable kinetochore-microtubule attachments.
source: In contrast, cells co-expressing mCherry-GBP-PP1γ and Astrin-∆70-GFP or −4A-GFP display cold stable kinetochore-microtubule attachments, demonstrating a successful restoration of attachment stability in Astrin-∆70 or −4A mutant expressing cells by delivering PP1γ (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, right).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cold stability assays shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The delivery of PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80 is sufficient to promote the kinetochore enrichment of Astrin-SKAP complex and stabilisation of end-on attachments.
source: In summary, these findings show that the delivery of PP1 near the C-terminus of Ndc80 is sufficient to promote the kinetochore enrichment of Astrin-SKAP complex and stabilisation of end-on attachments (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is concluded from rescue experiments with GBP-PP1.

claim: Depletion of Astrin did not abrogate SKA3 localisation at congressed kinetochores.
source: Depletion of Astrin did not abrogate SKA3 localisation at congressed kinetochores (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: In Astrin -∆70 or −4A expressing cells, depleted of endogenous Astrin, SKA3 recruitment was unperturbed at congressed kinetochores.
source: Similarly, in Astrin -∆70 or −4A expressing cells, depleted of endogenous Astrin, SKA3 recruitment was unperturbed at congressed kinetochores (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: SKA complex enrichment is not linked to Astrin enrichment at the kinetochore.
source: In conclusion, SKA complex enrichment is not linked to Astrin enrichment at the kinetochore.
evidence: This is concluded from observations that SKA3 localizes normally in Astrin mutant expressing cells.

claim: The failure to deliver PP1 by Astrin weakens KT-MT attachment stability without abrogating SKA complex recruitment at kinetochores.
source: Thus, the failure to deliver PP1 by Astrin weakens KT-MT attachment stability without abrogating SKA complex recruitment at kinetochores.
evidence: This is concluded from observations that Astrin mutants have attachment defects but normal SKA3 localization.

claim: Despite the inhibition of Aurora-B, there was no kinetochore enrichment of 4A or ∆70 mutants in monopolar spindles.
source: However, despite the inhibition of Aurora-B, there was no kinetochore enrichment of 4A or ∆70 mutants in monopolar spindles (Figure 7A,B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments combining Aurora-B inhibition with Astrin mutant expression shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing Astrin-4A or -∆70 displayed a higher proportion of laterally-attached kinetochores compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells.
source: In agreement, Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing Astrin-4A or -∆70 displayed a higher proportion of laterally-attached kinetochores compared to Astrin-WT expressing cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Inhibiting Aurora-B does not stabilise end-on attachments in the absence of Astrin:PP1 interaction.
source: These findings show that inhibiting Aurora-B does not stabilise end-on attachments in the absence of Astrin:PP1 interaction, showing the significance of Astrin:PP1 in stabilising KT-MT attachments.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that Aurora-B inhibition cannot rescue Astrin mutant defects.

claim: Co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ rescued the kinetochore localisation defect of both mutants (Astrin-4A-GFP and Astrin-∆70-GFP) in monopolar spindles of cells treated with Aurora-B inhibitor.
source: Co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ rescued the kinetochore localisation defect of both mutants (Astrin-4A-GFP and Astrin-∆70-GFP) in monopolar spindles of cells treated with Aurora-B inhibitor (compare Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and Figure 7E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through rescue experiments shown in Figure 7D,E.

claim: The co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ increased the incidence of end-on attachments in Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing either Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP.
source: In addition, the co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ increased the incidence of end-on attachments in Aurora-B inhibited cells expressing either Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP (Figure 7D; compare Figure 7F and C).
evidence: This is quantified from attachment status analysis shown in Figure 7D,F.

claim: The stabilisation of end-on attachments following the inhibition of Aurora-B is acutely dependant on the delivery of PP1 by Astrin.
source: These data show that the stabilisation of end-on attachments following the inhibition of Aurora-B is acutely dependant on the delivery of PP1 by Astrin.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that PP1 delivery is required even when Aurora-B is inhibited.

claim: In the presence of Aurora-B activity (DMSO-treated cells), the co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ is insufficient to rescue both the kinetochore localisation and attachment defects of Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP expressing cells.
source: In the presence of Aurora-B activity (DMSO-treated cells), the co-expression of mCherry-GBP-PP1γ is insufficient to rescue both the kinetochore localisation and attachment defects of Astrin-4A-GFP or Astrin-∆70-GFP expressing cells (Figure 7E,F and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C)
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: Both Astrin-PP1 and Aurora-B control KT-MT attachment status.
source: showing that both Astrin-PP1 and Aurora-B control KT-MT attachment status
evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that both Aurora-B inhibition and PP1 delivery are required for attachment stability.

claim: Cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing Astrin-WT-GFP disassembled monopolar asters normally to build bipolar spindles within 2 hr after STLC-release.
source: When STLC and Aurora-B inhibiting drugs were washed off, cells depleted of endogenous Astrin and expressing Astrin-WT-GFP, disassembled monopolar asters normally to build bipolar spindles within 2 hr (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is observed in time-lapse microscopy experiments shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: 45 min after STLC-release, cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed Astrin-WT-GFP enrichment on paired kinetochores.
source: In contrast, 45 min after STLC-release, cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed Astrin-WT-GFP enrichment on paired kinetochores (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: This is observed in fixed-cell analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Greater than 60% of Astrin depleted cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed unaligned chromosomes.
source: Importantly, time-lapse movies showed that greater than 60% of Astrin depleted cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed unaligned chromosomes (Figure 8A; n = 56 cells)
evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: ~54% of anaphase cells coexpressing Astrin-WT-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ displayed lagging chromosomes and a delayed anaphase onset.
source: and ~54% of anaphase cells displayed lagging chromosomes and a delayed anaphase onset (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B,C,D; n = 24 cells)
evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B,C,D.

claim: There is a need for a dynamic interaction between Astrin and PP1.
source: These observations highlight the need for a dynamic interaction between Astrin and PP1.
evidence: This is concluded from observations that constitutive PP1 delivery causes defects.

claim: Astrin-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells were significantly delayed in congressing chromosomes compared to Astrin-GFP alone expressing cells.
source: Analysing the rate of chromosome congression in cells presenting clear monopolar spindles showed that Astrin-GFP and mCherry-GBP-PP1γ co-expressing cells were significantly delayed in congressing chromosomes compared to Astrin-GFP alone expressing cells (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is quantified from time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of attachment stability leading to a delay in chromosome congression and anaphase onset and also errors in chromosome segregation.
source: These findings show that the constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of attachment stability leading to a delay in chromosome congression and anaphase onset and also errors in chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments with constitutive PP1 delivery.

claim: Two important sequential steps drive the rapid and selective stabilisation of end-on attachments: first, the reduction of Aurora-B activity allows the formation of end-on attachments and the initial recruitment of Astrin-sleeves at the kinetochore. Next, Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1, near the C-terminus of Ndc80, promotes its own enrichment as Astrin-crescents.
source: In summary, two important sequential steps drive the rapid and selective stabilisation of end-on attachments: first, the reduction of Aurora-B activity allows the formation of end-on attachments and the initial recruitment of Astrin-sleeves at the kinetochore. Next, Astrin-mediated delivery of PP1, near the C-terminus of Ndc80, promotes its own enrichment as Astrin-crescents - this positive feedback stabilises end-on attachments to withstand microtubule-mediated pulling (Figure 9).
evidence: This is the main mechanistic conclusion summarized from all experimental observations and illustrated in Figure 9.

claim: Although the inhibition of Aurora-B is essential for the formation of end-on attachment, it is insufficient to stabilise attachments in the absence of Astrin-mediated PP1 delivery.
source: Although the inhibition of Aurora-B is essential for the formation of end-on attachment, it is insufficient to stabilise attachments in the absence of Astrin-mediated PP1 delivery.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments showing that Aurora-B inhibition cannot rescue Astrin mutant defects.

claim: Constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of KT-MT attachment stability causing delayed chromosome congression and defective anaphase.
source: Conversely, constitutive delivery of PP1 by Astrin disrupts the dynamic regulation of KT-MT attachment stability causing delayed chromosome congression and defective anaphase.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments with constitutive PP1 delivery.

claim: Astrin-PP1 interaction acts as a dynamic lock that rapidly and selectively stabilises mature kinetochore-microtubule attachments to ensure the accurate segregation of chromosomes.
source: Thus, Astrin-PP1 interaction acts as a dynamic lock that rapidly and selectively stabilises mature kinetochore-microtubule attachments to ensure the accurate segregation of chromosomes.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on all experimental observations.
